Reasoning first: a JavaScript Number is an IEEE 754 double with a 53-bit significand, so it represents integers exactly only up to 2^53 (9,007,199,254,740,992). 2^61 − 17 is about 2.3 × 10^18, far above that, and it is odd, so it needs more than 53 bits and a Number would round it. The product, about 6.9 × 10^18, has the same problem. The fix is BigInt, using `2n ** 61n - 17n` and `* 3n` with BigInt literals throughout. Mixing BigInt and Number in one expression throws a TypeError, so every operand has to be a BigInt.
